### Problems found

**1 blocker, 2 warnings.**

**RUN-03** · blocker · [Verified]
There is no start command. `package.json` has `build` and `test` scripts but no `start`.
Azure App Service needs to know how to run your app. Without a start command it guesses,
and the guess is usually wrong — the deploy will appear to work but the site will not come
up.
**Fix:** add a `start` script to `package.json`, for example
`"start": "node dist/index.js"`.

**RUN-04** · warning · [Verified]
No health endpoint (`/health`, `/healthz`) was found.
Without one, the workflow cannot confirm the app actually responds after deploying, so a
broken deploy still reports green.
**Fix:** add a route that returns HTTP 200, then re-run `/deploy-check` so the workflow
gains a health-check step.

**BUILD-05** · warning · [Assumed]
The build output folder could not be determined. No framework was detected, so the usual
conventions (`dist/`, `build/`) cannot be assumed safely.
**Fix:** confirm where `npm run build` writes its output and check the `package:` path in
the workflow matches.

*Checks not applicable here: all `DOCK-*` (no Dockerfile), all `DATA-*` (no database
configuration or migrations found).*

## 2. How does the deployment work?

In plain terms: when you push code to `main`, GitHub builds your app and copies the result
to Azure.

Step by step, each time it runs:

1. You push code to the `main` branch.
2. GitHub Actions starts the workflow in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
3. It checks out your code and installs Node 22.
4. It installs dependencies with `npm ci`.
5. It builds the app with `npm run build`.
6. It signs in to Azure using the publish profile stored in your GitHub secrets.
7. It uploads the built files to the App Service named `vilje-api-prod`.

**If any step fails, the run stops and later steps do not happen.** A failed build never
reaches Azure.

Note: there is no automatic health check after step 7, because no health endpoint was
found (see RUN-04). The run will go green once the files are uploaded, even if the app
itself does not start. Until that is fixed, check the site yourself after each deploy.

---

## 3. What do I need to configure?

Everything here is done by a person, once, before the first deployment.

### GitHub secrets

Add these at: your repository → **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions** →
**New repository secret**.

> Secret **values** are never shown in this document and must never be pasted into chat or
> committed to the repository.

| Secret name | What to put in it | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| `AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE` | The contents of the publish profile file | Azure portal → your Web App → **Get publish profile** (downloads a file) → open it in a text editor and copy everything |

### Azure resources

These must exist before the first run. **[Unknown]** — the skill has no access to your
Azure account and cannot check whether any of them already exist.

| Resource | Name to use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| App Service (Web App) | `vilje-api-prod` | Runtime stack must be Node 22 to match `engines.node` |

**Publish profile setup**

1. Open the Azure portal and go to your Web App.
2. Click **Get publish profile** in the top toolbar. A file downloads.
3. Open that file in a text editor and copy its entire contents.
4. Paste it into the GitHub secret named `AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE`.

If the publishing credentials are ever reset in Azure, the profile changes and you must
download it again and update the secret. Deployments fail with an authentication error
until you do.

### Pre-deployment checklist

Tick every box before the first push.

- [ ] Fix RUN-03 — add a `start` script to `package.json`
- [ ] Confirm where `npm run build` writes output, and that the workflow's `package:` path matches (BUILD-05)
- [ ] App Service `vilje-api-prod` exists and is running
- [ ] Its runtime stack is set to Node 22
- [ ] The GitHub secret `AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE` has been added
- [ ] Someone has read `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` and agrees with what it does

## 4. How do I run the deployment?

1. Finish the checklist in section 3.
2. Commit your changes.
3. Push to the `main` branch:

   ```
   git push origin main
   ```

4. Open the **Actions** tab of the repository on GitHub. A run named
   **Deploy to Azure App Service** appears within a few seconds.

You can also start it by hand from the Actions tab: select the workflow, then click
**Run workflow**.

**No one needs to run any Azure command to deploy.** The workflow does that. The Azure
setup in section 3 is one-time.

---

## 5. How do I know whether it succeeded?

### Where to look

1. Open the **Actions** tab of this repository on GitHub.
2. Click the most recent run of **Deploy to Azure App Service**.
3. A green tick means every step passed. A red cross means it stopped — click the failed
   step to read the log.
4. When it is green, open `https://vilje-api-prod.azurewebsites.net` to check the app is
   actually serving.

Step 4 matters here: because there is no health check (RUN-04), a green run only proves
the files were uploaded, not that the app started.

### What this skill already checked

| Check | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| YAML parses | Passed | `deploy.yml` is valid YAML |
| Required workflow keys | Passed | `on:` and `jobs:` present, job declares a runner |
| Permissions scope | Passed | `contents: read` only — least privilege |
| Auth method | Passed | Publish profile, used with App Service — a valid combination |
| Action versions pinned | Passed | No action follows a moving branch such as `@main` |
| No inline secrets | Passed | Credentials are `${{ secrets.NAME }}` references only |
| Trigger scope | Passed | Runs only on pushes to `main`, not every branch |
| Concurrency | Passed | Two pushes cannot deploy at the same time |

**Not performed** — these were not checked, and why:

| Not checked | Reason |
|---|---|
| Expression and context errors | `actionlint` is not installed on this machine |
| App Service `vilje-api-prod` exists, with the right runtime | No Azure access |
| The publish profile secret is present and current | No access to repository settings |
| The application starts and serves traffic | Nothing was executed |
| Build and tests actually pass | `--run-build` was not set |

> YAML validation confirms syntax and structure only. It does not prove the deployment
> will succeed. Azure resources, permissions, quotas and network paths are unverified.

### If it fails — common causes

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow fails at the deploy step with an authentication error | The publish profile secret is missing, wrong, or was invalidated by a credential reset in Azure | Download the publish profile again and update `AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE` |
| Workflow is green but the site shows an error page | No start command (RUN-03) — App Service does not know how to run the app | Add a `start` script, then push again |
| Workflow is green but the site shows the default Azure welcome page | The `package:` path points at the wrong folder (BUILD-05) | Check where `npm run build` writes, update the workflow |
| Deploy step fails with "app not found" | The App Service name does not match `vilje-api-prod`, or it is in a different subscription | Confirm the name in the Azure portal and update the workflow |
| Build fails with a Node version error | The App Service runtime stack is not Node 22 | Set the runtime stack to Node 22 in the portal |
